findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Submodule.lean:64 `lemma asAlgebraHom_mem_of_forall_mem (p : Submodule k V) (hp : ∀ g, ∀ v ∈ p, ρ g v ∈ p) (v : V) (hv : v ∈ p) (x : k[G]) : ρ.asAlgebraHom x v ∈ p`, over `[CommSemiring k] [Monoid G] [AddCommMonoid V] [Module k V]`. That module is already publicly imported through TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/PermutationForm.lean:8, which the new file gets via Specht/Module.lean → PermutationModule/Form.lean, so no import change is needed.
findings.fix: Delete the lemma (and its proof via `asAlgebraHom_columnAntisymmetrizer_apply`) and inline at line 243-244: `hκ ▸ Representation.asAlgebraHom_mem_of_forall_mem _ U.toSubmodule (fun g _ hv => U.apply_mem_toSubmodule g hv) v hvU (columnAntisymmetrizer t)`.
findings.issue: `asAlgebraHom_columnAntisymmetrizer_mem` is Mathlib's `Representation.asAlgebraHom_mem_of_forall_mem` specialized to `x := columnAntisymmetrizer t`; its proof uses no property of the column antisymmetrizer, and it has a single consumer (line 244).

summary: One new declaration is a pure instantiation of an existing Mathlib lemma: `asAlgebraHom_columnAntisymmetrizer_mem` is `Representation.asAlgebraHom_mem_of_forall_mem` applied to `columnAntisymmetrizer t`. The rest of the file (James's Lemma 4.6 at module level, self-adjointness of `b_t`, the submodule theorem, irreducibility) is genuinely new and reuses the existing symmetrizer, factorization and tabloid-form API.
